brief: DWS's CIO Flash frames the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% (first since 2023, unanimous) as a credibility move rather than the start of an extended tightening cycle. Inflation has stayed above the Fed's 2% target for over five years: August headline CPI rose 0.4% (3.4% y/y, gasoline over a third of the gain) and core CPI rose 0.3% (annual core easing to 2.4%), with oil above USD 100 adding pass-through risk. Labor data stayed firm (payrolls +162,000, unemployment 4.1%, retail sales +1.2%) even as consumer sentiment fell to its second-lowest reading on record. DWS traces Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's tone from June's guidance pullback through a hawkish Jackson Hole stance stressing inflation credibility over rate-sensitive weakness, comparing his approach to Greenspan's risk-management style and the pre-emptive 1994-95 tightening cycle. The median dot plot points to one more 2026 hike; 2027 views diverge. DWS calls this fine-tuning, not recalibration, driven mainly by credibility given bond pricing and oil, and favors selective duration while viewing one or two more hikes as tolerable for equities, with AI beneficiaries seen as resilient.
